html:
The Shuar and the Wampis (Huambisa) are two related Jivaroan peoples of the Amazon foothills of the Andes, the Shuar in south-eastern Ecuador and the Wampis across the border in Peru. Older books called them Jívaro.

They lived in scattered households in the forest, farming manioc, hunting and fishing, and were famous warriors. The Inca ruler Huayna Capac failed to conquer them, and in 1599 they rose against Spanish gold-mining towns in their land and destroyed them. For centuries they kept outsiders out. They are known abroad for the tsantsa, the shrunken head of an enemy, made in war rituals.

In 1964 the Shuar formed one of the first Indigenous federations in South America. In 2015 the Wampis declared their own autonomous territorial government in Peru. Neighbours include the Sápara.
